indra: Hey team — hitting nondeterministic evals bringing up quant-7b-q8. Same seed across runs but outputs differ between local and CI. Anyone seen this?

maya: Yep, noticed instability on the metric dashboard this morning. Same prompt+seed, CI variance ~4-6% on exact-match. :eyes:

indra: Repro steps:
```
# local
python -m eval_runner --seed 1337 --model redwood/quant-7b-q8 --batch 4 --top_p 0.95 --temp 0.0
# CI (docker image)
docker run --rm -e SEED=1337 ghcr.io/redwood-inference/eval:quant-7b-q8 python -m eval_runner --seed 1337 --model redwood/quant-7b-q8 --batch 4 --top_p 0.95 --temp 0.0
```
Both runs produced different token sequences (not just spacing). Example snippet: 
```
# local first sample tokens: "In summary, the answer is Paris ."
# CI first sample tokens:    "The city of Paris is the capital of France ."
```

sam: Two quick suspects: 1) sampling config mutations (we were copying the sampling dict shallowly in the runner) so annealing code might mutate a shared object across requests. 2) entropy/getrandom behavior in container vs host — if workers are forked they can share RNG state.

maya: I dug in — CI image is built on an image that uses musl / different glibc behavior and we spawn worker subprocesses via fork+exec in the runner pool. Pattern: main process seeds RNG then forks N workers — if the seeding happens before fork, you can get identical RNG streams or subtle differences depending on libc getrandom semantics.

ci-bot: [run 2026-03-18T09:12:10Z] eval-quant-7b-q8 #423 failed metric-regression check (delta=5.1%)

olivia: Proposed fixes:
- Make per-worker deterministic seeding explicit. Derive worker seed = HMAC_SHA256(global_seed, worker_id) -> int, then create per-worker RNG with numpy.random.default_rng(worker_seed). Avoid relying on os.urandom or inherited RNG state.
- Copy sampling config per request (sampling_cfg = copy.deepcopy(base_cfg)) before annealing so we don't mutate shared objects.
- In CI, set PYTHONHASHSEED and PYTHONUTF8=1 for parity, and add a small smoke test that runs the same seed 3x inside the docker image to detect nondet runs.

indra: That sounds good. I'll draft a tiny patch: set explicit worker seeding, deep-copy sampling cfg, and add a smoke test in the eval runner test matrix. Will also add a CI step to run the smoke test inside the built image before publishing.

sam: One more thing — add an integration test that asserts identical token stream for 5 repeats with the same seed. If it flaps, fail the job early. This should catch weird OS-level entropy differences.

maya: I can repro locally by toggling the forking mode:
```
# deterministic (works)
python -m eval_runner --seed 1337 --worker-mode spawn ...
# flaky (fork)
python -m eval_runner --seed 1337 --worker-mode fork ...
```
So put explicit docs and default to spawn in CI for now.

indra: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/pull/248 (WIP) — will add tests and CI smoke.

olivia: Nice. After PR, let's run full quantized model evals overnight and see whether metric variance drops. Also file a follow-up to ensure docker base image uses same libc as our recommended stack.

sam: Agreed. Also add a small note in onboarding docs about "deterministic bring-up checklist" (seed handling, sampling immutability, worker-mode) — otherwise future model brings will hit the same trap. :+1:

indra: Thanks — will update this thread when PR is green.
